card.name: Inside long drug and medical names
card.fires_on: A middle piece of a long drug or medical word that is split into parts, such as benzodiaz-EP-ines, f-ES-oterodine, SPRA-V-ATO or conj-UNCT-iva. It fires where the rest of the word still has to be completed.

modes.label: Benzodiazepine split
modes.description: The middle piece 'ep' or 'EP' inside the word benzodiazepine(s).
modes.example: CONCOMITANT USE WITH BENZODIAZ<<EP>>INES OR OTHER CNS DEPRESSANTS;

modes.label: Other drug brand/generic names
modes.description: A middle piece inside a drug name such as fesoterodine, SPRAVATO or XERAVA.
modes.example: The recommended starting dosage of f<<es>>oterodine fumarate extended-release

modes.label: Other medical terms
modes.description: A middle piece inside terms like bilirubin or conjunctiva.
modes.example: Close the conj<<unct>>iva with 6-0 plain gut

card.writes: It mostly pushes unrelated tokens such as ' away' and Japanese endings while suppressing word endings like 'ert' and 'ort', so the output effect is unclear.
card.plain: It lights up in the middle of a long drug or medical word that is split into pieces, before the word is finished.
